info.name: MetalCharts API
info.description:
Live and historical prices for precious and base metals, plus the exchange data behind them: COMEX warehouse inventory and deliveries, LBMA vaults and clearing, Shanghai SGE and SHFE, India MCX premiums, Guangzhou GFEX warehouse receipts, and CFTC Commitments of Traders positioning. Commercial use is permitted on every plan including the free tier, which allows 200 requests a month. On the free tier, any public display of the data must show a visible link to https://metalcharts.org, such as "Metal prices by MetalCharts"; free-tier responses carry an X-Attribution header saying so. Paid plans need no link.

## Setup

1. Get a free API key at https://metalcharts.org/metals-api (200 requests a month, no card).
2. Open the collection's Variables tab and set `apiKey` to your key (`mc_live_...`). Put it in the Current value column so it stays on your machine and is not synced or shared.
3. Send any request. Auth is set once on the collection: `Authorization: Bearer {{apiKey}}`.

Optional parameters are listed on each request but switched off; tick them to use them.

- API reference: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs
- Pricing: https://metalcharts.org/api-pricing
- OpenAPI 3.0 document: https://api.metalcharts.org/docs/json
- Code examples: https://github.com/maxcash2147/metalcharts-api-examples

A `date` counts as history: Free reaches 30 days back, paid plans their history depth.

request.description:
Holds the connection open and sends text/event-stream. The first event is `snapshot` with every requested symbol (`data: {"data": {"XAU": {...}}, "timestamp": "..."}`), then a `price` event (`data: {"symbol": "XAU", ...quote}`) each time a quote changes. A `: ping` comment arrives about every 15 seconds. The server may close the stream at any time, so clients should reconnect with backoff.

Concurrent connections: Pro 1, Ultimate 10, Enterprise 50. Other plans get a 403 with `required_plan`, and one connection too many gets a 429.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

request.description:
Historical price series for a metal. Symbols are the metal codes, not names: XAU (gold), XAG (silver), XPT (platinum), XPD (palladium), HG (copper), plus ALI, NI, ZN, PB, JBP, CO, LC and UXA.`GOLD` is not valid here; it belongs to /v1/markets. Use the range parameter (for example 1M, 6M, 1Y or ALL; MAX is accepted as a synonym for ALL) or a start date to set the window; start overrides range, and end (used only with start) defaults to now. interval picks the candle size. Supported intervals are 15m, 30m, 45m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 1d, 1w and 1M; intraday intervals read the interval candle tables and 1w/1M are aggregated from daily candles. Prices are in US dollars per the market's own unit unless currency, unit or karat say otherwise; each point is converted at the ECB reference rate in force on its date (FX history starts 1999-01-04, and earlier points are left out of a converted series). The response states the currency and unit it is in.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

query.description: Comma-separated metal codes. Default: all of XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD, HG, ALI, NI, ZN, PB, JBP, CO, LC, UXA.

request.description:
Every daily bar for the requested metals, back to the start of each series (October 1966 for gold and silver), as one CSV file with columns symbol, date, open, high, low, close, volume, currency, unit. `currency` and `unit` convert as on /v1/history (FX history starts 1999-01-04, so a converted file starts there). For an initial load or a nightly sync. Requires the Ultimate plan.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

request.description:
Latest Shanghai Gold Exchange spot prices and premium to Western pricing. `price` is USD per troy ounce, `priceCNY` is in the exchange's native unit (CNY/kg for silver, CNY/g for gold), and `exchangeRate` is USD/CNY. Shanghai silver prices (SGE and SHFE) include China's VAT and are returned as quoted; `priceExVat`, `priceCNYExVat` and `premiumPercentExVat` strip it at `vatRate`, and `vatInclusive` says whether a price carries VAT. Gold carries none, so its ex-VAT fields equal the raw ones.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

request.description:
Daily COMEX warehouse stocks and flows per depository, laid out like CME's metal depository statistics report: for registered, eligible and total metal, the previous stock, received, withdrawn, net change, adjustment and today's stock. Rows are per report date, with activityDate giving the business day the movements happened. Received, withdrawn and adjustment are null on report dates before flowsAvailableFrom; stocks go back to February 2026 for most metals. Use /v1/comex/inventory for the exchange-wide totals, which go back to 1992 for gold and silver. Requires the Pro plan or higher.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

Every instrument the platform tracks, with the exchange and asset class it belongs to. Use this to discover the symbol a given endpoint expects: symbol spaces differ per route, so gold is XAU on /v1/history but GOLD on /v1/markets, and commodities are contract codes such as CL1. request.description:
Retail bullion prices across competing dealers, with each quote's premium over spot. Every product is normalised to its fine-ounce content so premiums are comparable across coins, bars and junk silver. `best` is the cheapest in-stock quote at or above spot, falling back to the cheapest such quote; a below-spot quote stays in `quotes` but is never `best`, and `best` is null when every fresh quote is below spot. Premium is the figure recorded at scrape time and travels with its own scrapedAt, so price and premium always agree. Filter with metal: gold, silver, platinum or palladium, or the code each product carries in `metal` (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD), in any case. Quotes older than 7 days are excluded by default and never chosen as `best`, because individual dealer scrapers fail silently and a stale row would otherwise be presented as today's cheapest price; widen or narrow that with max_age_days, and read `asOf`, `ageDays` and `staleQuotesExcluded` to judge freshness yourself. Requires the Pro plan or higher.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs

Latest perpetual funding rate for every symbol, optionally scoped to one venue. Funding is the periodic payment between longs and shorts that holds a perpetual near spot: a positive rate means longs pay shorts, so the sign and size read directly as crowd positioning. Rates are per-interval decimals, so 0.0000125 is 0.00125%. Coverage includes GOLD and SILVER perps alongside crypto and tokenised equities. Requires the Pro plan or higher.

Plans, limits and the full field list: https://metalcharts.org/metals-api/docs
